test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which financial products are commonly offered by Microfinance Institutions in India?

options.text: Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals

solution:
The correct answer is __**Savings, credit and insurance services tailored for low-income individuals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in India primarily provide **financial products and services** to economically disadvantaged groups, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• The main offerings include **savings accounts**, small-value loans (microcredit), and **micro-insurance products** tailored to the needs of low-income individuals.
 
• MFIs often focus on promoting **financial inclusion** by offering these services to populations that lack access to traditional banking systems.
 
• Micro-loans are typically **unsecured** and range from a few thousand rupees to assist individuals in starting or expanding small businesses.
 
• MFIs may also provide financial literacy programs to help beneficiaries better manage their resources and improve their economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microcredit:** Small loans provided to individuals or groups without requiring collateral, often used for income-generating activities or small businesses.
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs):** Many MFIs work with SHGs, which are community-based groups that pool savings and access microfinance services collectively.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** The process of ensuring access to financial services like savings, credit, and insurance to all segments of society, particularly vulnerable and low-income groups.
 
• **Key Players in Indian Microfinance:** Some prominent MFIs in India include SKS Microfinance, Bandhan Bank, Ujjivan Financial Services, and Spandana Sphoorty.
 
• **Regulation of MFIs:** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates MFIs and has set guidelines for their functioning, including interest rate caps and loan repayment structures.
